newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate begins state/municipal debt probe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate begins state/municipal debt probe.

text.p: A special investigating committee in the Brazilian Senate began hearings into allegedly fraudulent operations by state and municipal governments involving debt issues, an official said.
The Parliamentary Commission of Enquiry (CPI) was due to investigate four states -- Alagoas, Pernambuco, Santa Catarina and Sao Paulo.
The states supposedly broke constitutional rules by seeking authorisation for debt issues to cover court order indemnities which were exaggerated or never existed, the official said.

Senator Vilson Kleinubing, who first brought the allegations up in the Senate, showed a Central Bank document which said nearly $2 billion had been raised by the four states and the municipalities of Campinas, Osasco and Guarulhos, all in Sao Paulo state, via such operations in 1995 and 1996.
The senator said he did not know how much of that total may have been raised fraudulently.
Brazil's constitution stipulates that state and municipal governments must seek Senate and Central Bank approval before issuing debt to cover costs incurred by court order decisions.
Kleinubing also said the investigation would also probe the sale of debt on secondary markets. The scope of the investigation is limited to 1995 and 1996.
